children.value: A neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs and passes it through a nonlinear activation function. A single layer of perceptrons separates classes only with hyperplanes and cannot compute XOR; a hidden layer computes a new representation in which the classes become separable.

Neural network research came in three waves: perceptrons from 1958, backpropagation from 1986, and deep learning from 2006, which won with large datasets, graphics processors, and the training techniques of C.3.

Training minimizes a loss with stochastic gradient descent on mini-batches, usually with momentum. Backpropagation computes all partial derivatives in one backward pass: the delta of a neuron is the derivative of the loss with respect to its sum, hidden deltas come from the deltas of the next layer, and each weight’s gradient is its input times the delta it feeds.

Sigmoid derivatives of at most 1/4 make gradients vanish in deep networks, and large weights make them explode. ReLU-type activations, He initialization, normalization layers, and residual connections keep signals and gradients at a stable scale.

Regularization fights overfitting: more data through augmentation and self-supervised pretraining, early stopping, weight decay, and dropout. Adam adapts the step size of each parameter to the size of its gradients.
Convolutional layers connect each neuron to a local receptive field and share the kernel across all positions. Stride and padding set the output size, pooling summarizes neighborhoods,

The architectures from LeNet to ResNet made convolutional networks deeper and cheaper: small kernels, inception modules, residual connections, and dense connections. The Vision Transformer replaces convolutions with attention over image patches.

Recurrent networks process sequences with a hidden state and are trained with backpropagation through time, where gradients vanish over long distances. LSTM and GRU cells keep information with gated additive updates; attention, and finally the transformer, removed the need for recurrence.
